ov: A wild sheep of western North America named for its large horns. Its ancestors crossed from Siberia over the Bering land bridge. In the rut, rams lunge into head-butts, and their skulls are built to absorb the impact.
rg: Western North America, from southwestern Canada to Mexico.
df: Grasses and shrubs; it also seeks out natural salt licks.
fx: A ram’s horns can weigh 14 kg, as much as all the bones in its body.
By 1900 the population had crashed to a few thousand from livestock diseases and overhunting.
